checks.label: In a QH-curve a low flow results in a high head and a high flow results in a low head: the example pump's curve runs through all five tests and falls the whole way, from 21 m at 0 m³/h to 14 m at 20 m³/h, and every screen draws it

Choosing a flow rate on the horizontal axis, proceeding vertically to the pump curve and then left to the vertical axis reads the head: each up-then-across reading draws its line up from the flow to the curve and left to the head axis, 10 m³/h reading 19 m and 20 m³/h 14 m, and across from 17 m and down reads 15 m³/h

The highest head occurs at the lowest flow rate, and the highest flow rate occurs at the lowest head: on the tested curve the highest head, 21 m, is at the lowest flow, 0 m³/h, and the lowest head, 14 m, at the highest tested flow, 20 m³/h, which the no-flow puzzle reads as 21 m

Starting on the wrong axis is drawn as it reads: from 20 on the head axis when the head at 20 m³/h is wanted, across and down reads 5, the flow for a 20 m head; 20 put on the flow axis when the flow for 20 m is wanted reads 14 m; both in the warning colour

State the difference between interpolation and extrapolation and the limitations of each: a reading between two tests (12.5 m³/h, about 18 m) lies between their heads, while past the last test a ruler through the last two tests and the bend of the last three disagree, 11 m and 10 m at 25 m³/h and 8 m and 5 m at 30 m³/h, so there the graph gives only a guess

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is a named slip: starting on the wrong axis, the mark below, a gridline short, no flow read as no head, the head read as rising, the flow's change given, a reading past the tests trusted or read as measured
Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture and clear of each other, of the points and of the lines; each slip is drawn in the warning colour
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: no reading line, reading point, counted square or label, no shaded stretch, and the marker to drag starts at 0

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart
